purpose: Nystatin is used to treat fungal infections caused by a yeast called Candida. It can treat infections in your mouth (thrush), throat, intestines, and skin. It is not used for infections in your bloodstream or other serious internal infections.
how_it_works: Nystatin works by attaching to the outer wall of the fungal cells and poking holes in it. This causes the contents of the fungal cell to leak out, which kills the fungus. Because it works this way, it only kills fungus and does not harm your own body's cells.
common_side_effects: When used in the mouth or swallowed, it may cause nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or an upset stomach. When used on the skin, it can sometimes cause mild irritation, redness, or a burning sensation at the application site. These side effects are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to nystatin or any other medications before using it. If your symptoms do not improve after using nystatin as directed, contact your doctor, as you may have a different type of infection. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before using this medication, although it is generally considered safe when used as directed.
typical_dosing: For mouth infections (thrush), the liquid form is usually swished around in your mouth and then swallowed, 4 times a day. For skin infections, the cream or powder is applied to the affected area 2 to 3 times a day. Always follow the exact instructions your doctor gives you and finish the full course even if you feel better early.
